newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Australian minister says racism not raised in Asia.
newsitem.headline: Australian minister says racism not raised in Asia.

text.p: Australian Foreign Minister Alexander Downer said on Friday he had seen no repercussions from a heated debate on racism and immigration in his country while on a tour of three Asian nations.

Downer, speaking after meeting Indonesian President Suharto in Jakarta, said he himself had raised the issue three times during his trip, including once during a dinner with Malaysian Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad.

When asked if the racism issue had come up during the Suharto meeting or in discussions with Indonesian counterparts during a two-day Australia-Indonesia Ministerial Forum, Downer said: "It hasn't come up at all."

The race debate in Australia was sparked last month when politician Pauline Hanson made a parliamentary speech claiming the country was being swamped by Asians and that indigenous Aborigines were gaining unfair preferential treatment.
Prime Minister John Howard has said Australians of Asian background made up only 4.8 percent of the country's 18 million population.
Downer said he directly addressed the issue publicly twice earlier in the week in speeches to Malaysian alumni of Australian universities in Kuala Lumpur and at a public policy forum in New Delhi.
"I didn't do that in reaction to the question being raised. When I was in India I met the prime minister and three other ministers and none of them raised it with me," he said.

"I have addressed it because it is important that there is no doubt anywhere in the region where the Australian government stands but I must say in my official dealings I think there isn't any doubt where the Australian government stands," he said.

"We have made it clear in the region as well as in Australia that we abhor racism and we adhere to a non-discriminatory immigration policy. If we did otherwise, Australia would become quite isolated and we don't want that," Downer said.
Australia's debate on immigration and race has resurfaced in in recent weeks and has heightened racial tensions. On Wednesday, one town mayor called children of mixed-race marriages "mongrels".

Howard on Thursday defended Australia as a tolerant society, saying: "Australians are to be congratulated, not denigrated, for the extraordinary tolerance and decency (they) have demonstrated over the years to successive waves of migration from different parts of the world."
